untrustedWorkspaces.description: The reactive Quantbook kernel runs arbitrary workspace Python and is gated behind workspace trust. Other features work in Restricted Mode.

commandPalette._comment: W3 (Wave 3): the Cell Grid context-menu items are right-click-only. Hide them from the Command Palette -- their generic titles (Cut/Copy/Insert Row Above) are meaningful only in the grid's right-click menu, and they act on the focused grid (no palette affordance).
Wave G3a (R4): Hide/Unhide rows need the right-click context payload (panelToken + selection); hide from the palette like the structural + freeze commands.
Watchlist rename/delete/removeSymbol act on the right-clicked Data-tree node; they are meaningless without one.
M56: the History-tree pin/compare wrappers act on the right-clicked History-tree node; they are meaningless without one.

view/item/context._comment: M56: History-tree run entries. contextValue is status-aware -- quantlab.history.entry.<status> (HistoryTreeProvider.getTreeItem) -- so Cancel only shows on running/queued runs.

webview/context._comment: W3 (Wave 3): the Cell Grid right-click menu. Gated on the quantbook grid webview + the body-cell section (set via data-vscode-context on right-click). Excel-style groups: 1=clipboard, 2=clear, 3=format/freeze, 4=insert/delete. The conductor merges this section across the 3 wave-3 windows.
W3: routes to the frozen-panes lead's Freeze command. The command id is the W3-assumed name; the conductor reconciles it with the lead's actual id at integration (runtime-pending the lead's command).

Wave G3a (R4): Hide/Unhide rows over the selected span -- consumes the Wave G2 engine row-visibility substrate. Kept in the 4_structure cluster (row/column ops) after delete; the webview/context when only sees webviewId/webviewSection (no per-item dynamic enablement), so Unhide always appears and no-ops with an info toast when the span has no hidden rows.

FE-4 W2: sort the selected range by a key column. Group 5_data is the new data-ops group below structure (1=clipboard, 2=edit, 3=format, 4=structure, 5=data). Palette-visible (NOT in the commandPalette when:false list).
FE-4 W1: Define Name over the right-clicked selection. New group 6_names (after 4_structure) so it sits below insert/delete without renumbering W2/W3 groups.
FE-11: surface the existing Name Manager / Go-To-Name commands in the grid right-click (they were palette-only). Same 6_names group + same when as Define Name.

FE-8: structured-table lifecycle from the grid right-click. Group 7_table (after 6_names). Create reads the right-clicked selection as the footprint; Rename/Drop resolve the table CONTAINING the right-clicked cell (tableAtCell), else open a QuickPick. The host commands accept the data-vscode-context payload (panelToken + selection).

FE-8.1: Resize Table to Selection. Same 6_names-adjacent 7_table group + same when as the other table ops. Selection-driven (resolveMenuOrFocusedSelection): the target is the table whose top-left equals the selection's top-left.

FE-8.3: Rename Table Column. Same 7_table group + when as the other table ops. Context-aware (resolveTableTarget): renames a column of the table containing the right-clicked cell, or picks one from a QuickPick.

keybindings._comment: FE-4 W1: Replace All in the focused Cell Grid. Ctrl+H (Cmd+H on mac), the Sheets/Excel Replace convention. Scoped to the grid webview panel being active (activeWebviewPanelId == the grid viewType) so it never shadows the editor's own Find/Replace. Ctrl+F is NOT bound here -- the webview owns the in-sheet find bar (plan amendment 2026-06-10).

FE-11: Name Manager in the focused Cell Grid. Ctrl+F3 (Cmd+F3 on mac), Excel's Name Manager chord. The editor binds Ctrl+F3 to Find-Next-Selection, but that is editor-focus-scoped (kbExpr EditorContextKeys.focus); THIS binding is scoped to the grid webview panel being active (activeWebviewPanelId == the grid viewType), and those contexts are mutually exclusive, so they never collide. Go-To-Name is left to the menu / palette / name box (avoids the F5/Ctrl+G conflicts).

quantlab.pythonPath.description: Path to the Python interpreter for the qviz daemon (visualisation). When empty, Quantlab falls through to python.defaultInterpreterPath, then to ~/.quantlab/venv/bin/python. Setting an explicit path that does not resolve to an executable file fails loudly (does not silently fall through).

quantlab.quantbookMcpPort.description: FE-BEYOND B1: TCP port for the read-only Quantbook MCP server (bound to 127.0.0.1 only). 0 (the default) lets the OS pick a free port; the resolved URL is printed to the Quantbook MCP Server output channel on start.

quantlab.trading.consecutiveLossLimit.description: Maximum consecutive losing trades before automatic halt (Decision L74: 3).

quantlab.trading.maxExposure.description: Maximum total exposure in USD. Set 0 to disable.

quantlab.trading.maxPositionSize.description: Maximum position size (shares). Set 0 to disable.

quantlab.trading.maxOpenOrders.description: Maximum open orders across sessions. Set 0 to disable.

quantlab.notifications.showSessionStatus.description: Show notifications when sessions start, pause, or stop.

quantlab.notifications.playFillSound.description: Play a sound when trades are executed.
